lessons: LPASS macro and SoundWire codec patterns compose when the macro owns MMIO/clock-provider lifecycle and only removes vendor SoundWire notifications.
WSA macro adds regulator-like binding semantics (vdd-micb-supply) that should fail closed without exact same-class evidence.
Combined architecture needs separate scoring for macro-side SoundWire coupling; codec-side SDW slave patterns do not directly become macro code.
Clock-output-names remains the strongest deterministic signal for clock provider registration.
